messages:
sophie: quick heads-up — ran the nightly perf suite on the kernel-selector canary and saw a regression for small streaming requests (mostly 16-64 token payloads). p50 +12%, p95 +18%. flamegraphs point to host-side parsing + writev churn

mike: ugh. any obvious diffs from baseline? kernel-selector should only affect GPU-side scheduling, not host parse path

sophie: right. what we changed: selector will prefer 'compact-kernel-v2' for models with seq<=64. the runtime then changes framing slightly (smaller kv-prefetch hints). looks innocuous but the trace shows more frequent small write calls into grpc socket

elaine: can you paste the sampling lines?

sophie: paste of perf sample (top stacks collapsed):
```
host::ingress::parse_request -> tokenization::mini_tokenize -> preparse::fragment -> grpc::writev -> epoll_wait
host::kvcache::lookup -> kvcache::miss -> host::ingress::parse_request
```
count: writev spikes 3x vs baseline for the 16-64 token bench

max: that suggests fragment boundary behaviour caused by the kernel hint change — more micro-fragments so host issues extra flushes. grpc smallwrite penalties kill latency on p50.

perf-bot: perf-run: build=canary-ks-2024-04-#+42, bench=ingress-mini-stream, samples=1200, p50=48ms(+12%), p95=143ms(+18%)

mike: did we change batching heuristics too? smaller batches would mean more outgoing frames

sophie: no code change there. but the selector alters chosen kernel which changes kvcache expectations: the warmup prefetch no longer triggers early because compact-kernel-v2 expects shorter KV lifetimes. so we see more kvcache misses that cause an extra host-side walk per request

elaine: kvcache miss -> extra reads -> extra small writes? explain flow

sophie: sequence: request arrives -> parser splits into fragments -> tokenization emits a prefix that misses in kvcache -> runtime issues a synchronous KV fetch to metadata service (fast but adds syscall) -> on return the host now sends a small proto chunk to GPU/sidecar -> grpc writev flushes a ~80byte frame -> kernel kicks off compute. more of those per single request instead of one coalesced write

max: that matches the flamegraphs. mitigation options: 1) revert selector change, 2) re-enable prefetch hints for compact-kernel-v2, 3) coalesce writev at proxy layer, 4) tune batching window to aggregate those tiny writes

mike: can we add a cheap coalescer in the host proxy? buffer for ~200us then flush (configurable). low-risk and might help other smallwrite noise

elaine: we already have coalesce hooks in rust-proxy but they're disabled for low-latency paths. we can enable dynamic coalescing only when average payload < 256 bytes. needs perf test for tail latency impact

sophie: did a quick A/B in local sim: enabling coalescer reduces p50 back to baseline, p95 improved ~5%. CPU overhead ~+0.6% because of buffering logic.

infra-bot: FYI: kube canary deployment rolled ks-canary -> 6 pods, 1 region. no alerts yet.

max: besides coalescer we should address root cause: why does compact-kernel-v2 change kvcache hints? perhaps our kernel metadata contract drifted. @sophie can you open an issue to revert the selector until we patch hints?

sophie: filing issue now: https://redwood/issue/INF-3421 (revert-selector + investigation). also adding a perf test for small streaming requests.

mike: action items:
- sophie: revert canary or gate selector until hints fixed (INF-3421)
- elaine: enable dynamic coalescer behind feature flag + run e2e against canary
- max: add kvcache telemetry (miss rate by seq_len bucket) and smallwrite counters in host-proxy
- perf-bot: run nightly smoke with coalescer on/off to capture delta

elaine: I'll prototype the coalescer today. quick Q: what timeout did sophie use in the sim?

sophie: 200us window, and batch threshold 3 frames. tweakable.

max: for kvcache telemetry, please track: miss_count, cold_evictions, avg_lookup_ns, and correlate with selected_kernel. that'll help see selector->kvcache coupling

mike: also check HTTP/2 vs gRPC stacks — some customers use http gateway where semantics differ (writev vs single buffer). this regression might be less visible there.

sophie: noted. I ran both paths, gRPC showed the largest hit. http/1.1 path had smaller regression (~+4% p50)

elaine: ok will land the coalescer flag PR and run canary A/B. if it fixes, we keep and then unroll the selector change and fix hints in parallel

mike: sounds good. if anyone sees client errors or increased latency in canary region, ping #incidents immediately.

sophie: thanks all — will update INF-3421 with perf artifacts and next steps.
